RI-UIX03 §A pause rule: menu pauses OUTSIDE combat, runs at 60Hz INSIDE combat. UISystem.pausesSimulation(inCombat) = mode!=='world' && mode!=='dialogue' && !inCombat — a new 'map' mode inherits the correct rule for free.

AGENT-PROTOCOL: audit the LIVE WORLD after a load, not the blob — a written-never-read field re-serialises and passes forever. Vary WHEN you save, not just the seed.

Q7's TEXT is narrow: 'Any map, minimap, or map page IN OR REACHABLE FROM THE JOURNAL'. The EXISTENCE clause lives only in the JU8 scoring row ('map unreachable AND non-existent') and in method 7's second sentence ('the map must not exist at all') and in the 'how we lose' bullet. Map must still NOT be reachable from the journal — navigable() in journal mode must never contain 'map'.

ui/surface.js FORBIDDEN_KINDS already contains 'map','map_pin','quest_marker','waypoint','minimap','objective_tracker'. Do NOT add 'map' as an element kind — add new kinds (map_terrain/map_place/map_player/map_local) so the forbidden-kind census still reads 0.
UISurface.el(rec, draw) is the ONLY drawing path and it CLIPS to the declared rect — you cannot draw undeclared. So the map's census and its pixels cannot disagree.

pois.json: 42 places with pos[] and kind. terrain.json `sites` carry r_flat / r_falloff — the WORLD's own definition of each place's extent, so 'personally stood in' = inside the site's own radius, non-arbitrary and drawn from world data.

I followed that - the RI-UIX04 edit is a NOTICE block that changes no clause and says so, added only because a critic scoring JU8's existence clause verbatim would hard-fail a build that S35 requires, costing a round.

SUCCESSOR-2 RESUME: box is QUIET (pgrep headless_shell=0, loadavg 0.53) - the exact condition the predecessor was waiting for. All three gates clean on this quiet box BEFORE any of my changes: check-data 503/503 (503 not 500 - other agents added data since), check-quests 94, boot-check PASS including its new rendered_a_frame assertion.

S11 STILL FAILED on the confirming run, and the predecessor's 'fix' was WRONG. ROOT CAUSE (general, affects any agent driving a menu): while a menu pauses the world, engine._step() takes the paused branch, which calls input.latchForStep(sim.frame) but NEVER calls stepOnce() - so sim.frame IS FROZEN. pipeline.latchForStep fires a scripted event only when `e.f + scriptBase === frame`. scriptBase is the frame at the queueInputs call, which is the frozen frame. Therefore ANY scripted press at f>=1 is UNREACHABLE inside a paused menu - it is never fired and never even counted as dropped (the drop branch needs f+base < frame, which a frozen frame can never satisfy). Only f:0 lands. tools/harness/critic-w1-15.mjs:191 already uses `f: 0, press:['interact']` - that is the established pattern.

Press AND release at f:0 in the SAME latch is correct and clean, not a cancellation: latchForStep ORs both into pendingPress/pendingRelease, then computes pressed = pendingPress & ~held BEFORE released = pendingRelease & held. So the press edge fires that frame and the button ends released. A tap on a frozen frame.

CONSEQUENCE THE PREDECESSOR WOULD HAVE SHIPPED: tools/harness/map-shots.mjs used the same f:1/f:3 pattern for the LOCAL VIEW shot. That press never lands either, so the 'local view' screenshot would have been a picture of the WORLD view carrying a local-view caption - a quietly wrong artifact, exactly the failure mode the protocol warns about. Fixed in both files.

STRENGTHENED S11 CAUGHT A REAL ENGINE-WIDE DEFECT, and it is not a map bug. UISystem.build() returns early on the cache key `builtFrame === ctx.frame && lastMode === mode && lastTouchSig === sig`. But EVERY MENU PAUSES THE WORLD outside combat, and engine._step()'s paused branch never calls stepOnce(), so ctx.frame IS FROZEN for as long as any screen is up. Mode does not change. The touch signature does not change. Therefore NO focus change made by an actual button press on a paused screen can ever invalidate the layout - the screen is frozen on the frame it was opened.

MEASURED, through the real input pipeline only. MAP: confirm moves focus.map.view 'world'->'local' and the drawn terrain element still says view=world with rect 684,230,552,634 unchanged (province aspect 0.871, not the local view's 1.0). So the local view was UNREACHABLE IN THE ACTUAL GAME - S35's 'local view for the current cell' was not shipped, only wired. JOURNAL (not my piece, same defect): stick right moves focus.journal.page 0->1 and the drawn journal elements are byte-identical. A player turning a page sees nothing move. frame_at_open=0, frame_now=0, frame_frozen=true.

WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT: engine.uiFocus(), openMenu() and closeMenu() all call ui.build(ctx, TRUE), forcing a rebuild. Every probe that moves focus with uiFocus() therefore never sees the bug. Only input driven through the real pipeline exposes it - which is exactly why S11 was written to go through queueInputs rather than call UISystem._confirm() directly. The probe design decision is what found it.

FIX LANDED in game/src/ui/system.js: new module-level focusSignature(mode, focus) is appended to the build() cache key. A/B COUNTERFACTUAL taken by temporarily restoring the old key and re-running the SAME test, so the control is the real pre-fix code and not an argument. Journal chronicle->index, driven by the stick through the pipeline: focus_moved=true in BOTH runs; layout_changed=false pre-fix, true post-fix. Map confirm: element view 'world' pre-fix, 'local' post-fix, and the rect goes 552x634 (province aspect 0.871) -> 634x634 (local aspect 1.0).

THE BIGGEST DEFECT OF THE PIECE, AND MY OWN PROBE WAS HIDING IT. map-probe C1 rebuilds the model for its radius sweep - `sim.discovery = new Disc({field, player, env, doc: eng.data.mapUI, pois: eng.data.pois})` - and never puts the shipped one back. So EVERY check after C1 (C2, C3, C4, all of S, all of D, all of L) measured a model THE PROBE ITSELF WIRED, not the one engine.js constructs at boot. 30/30 green against an object the game does not use.

MEASURED, one fresh boot, same 12 real site centres, nothing else changed: SHIPPED model = 255 cells revealed, 0 places. REBUILT model (identical constructor, same eng.data) = 4571 cells, 12 places. So the shipped discovery map recorded a twentieth of the ground and COULD NEVER NAME A SINGLE PLACE - Discovery's #sites list was empty, so `hasPlace` was false everywhere forever. That is why both capture screenshots came back with an empty map and the line 'I have not written anything down yet'. THE SCREENSHOT IS WHAT CAUGHT IT: the probe could not, by construction.

ROOT CAUSE: engine.js constructs `new Discovery({... doc: this.data.mapUI || {}, pois: this.data.pois})` at a point where BOTH are still undefined. Discovery reads them ONLY in its constructor (minR/maxR from doc.reveal; #sites from o.pois.pois), so the fallbacks stick for the life of the run: minR=maxR=0 and an empty site list. At probe time eng.data.mapUI and eng.data.pois are both fully populated (reveal 40/450, 42 pois, 34 field sites) - the data is fine, the ORDER is wrong.
next_step: fix engine construction order; make the probe measure the SHIPPED model; re-verify; re-capture
notes_for_successor:
Decision taken: roads are NOT drawn on the map. S35 forbids 'a route, path, trail or line of any kind' and a drawn road is the first thing a hostile critic will call a line. Wayfinding stays with signposts (already in the world).
STATE AT HANDOVER: everything is built and verified EXCEPT the docs/shots PNGs. map-probe.mjs was 29/29 with S11 failing once on its own driver bug (now fixed, needs ONE more confirming run). All three --break self-tests go red correctly.
THE ONLY OUTSTANDING RISK is the capture pass: 48 headless_shell on four cores and other agents editing game/ every few minutes, which drops the shared capture browser mid-job (BUILD CHANGED in reports/runs/.capture/capd.log). tools/harness/map-shots.mjs now retries 3x per shot at 960x540 with 16 stops. If it still fails, wait for a quiet box rather than lowering the settle threshold - S34 says an unsettled frame is an error, never a quiet pass.
